title: Through the wall: a half-heard address
summary: Mira gives Leo the address of the Halcyon's last survivor in the snug behind the Bell's kitchen. Ines, scrubbing pans on the other side of a thin wall, catches the street and not the number. She passes the street to Rook. Next morning Rook sees Leo knock at a blue door, and tells Ines. Neither of them ever hears the number.

witness.truth: Old Sefton, the last survivor of the Halcyon, lives at 19 Ropewalk Row, behind the blue door.

boat.truth: Tom will take Leo out on the Petrel at slack water on Thursday to see where the Halcyon went down.

spine.scene: The Drowned Bell, the snug behind the kitchen, a wet afternoon

spine.text: A wet afternoon. Mira has taken Leo into the snug behind the Bell's kitchen and shut the door. On the other side of the wall Ines is scrubbing pans, and the wall is very thin.
You wanted someone who was on her. There's one left alive.
Who?
Old Sefton. Ship's boy, then. He lives at 19 Ropewalk Row, behind the blue door. Knock twice and wait; he's slow on the stair.
Does he talk about it?
To me. Once. Whether he'll talk to you, I can't say.

spine.hint: Mira warns Leo how to speak to an old man who lost all his friends in one night.

spine.text: In the kitchen, Ines has stopped scrubbing. She stands very still with a pan in her hands and her ear to the wall.
Thank you. I mean it.
Don't thank me. Go tomorrow, early, before the street's awake.

spine.hint: Mira tells Leo something of what the ship's boy was like as a lad.

spine.text: Mira opens the snug door. In the kitchen Ines is suddenly very busy with the pans.
Oh! Didn't hear you there. Tea, either of you?
No. I'm away up to the light before the tide.

spine.hint: Ines fishes for what the two of them were talking about; Mira gives her nothing.

spine.text: Mira goes out the back way. Ines turns to Leo with a bright smile.

spine.hint: Ines asks Leo leading questions about his plans for tomorrow.

spine.text: Just a walk. See the town.
Mind the Ropewalk end, love, the cobbles are murder in the wet.

spine.hint: Ines gives Leo directions round town he didn't ask for.

spine.text: Evening on the quay. Ines brings Rook his supper and, as ever, a story.
Our Leo's going calling tomorrow. Somewhere on Ropewalk, Mira told him, I'd swear to it. Who do we know on Ropewalk who'd talk about the Halcyon?
Half the Row's widows of her.

spine.hint: Rook and Ines go through the old families of the Row; neither is sure who Mira meant.

spine.text: I'll find out. I always find out.
That's what worries me.

spine.hint: Ines and Rook talk about the newcomer and whether he should be digging up the wreck at all.

spine.scene: The Drowned Bell, the taproom, night

spine.text: Night. Tom is back from fishing, salt to the elbows, at the bar with Rook and Leo. Ines pours.
Leo, friend. Thursday at slack water I'm taking the Petrel out for crab. Come along, and you'll see where she went down.
I'd like that.

spine.hint: Tom boasts about the Petrel; Ines worries aloud about the weather.

spine.text: Leo's got calls to make first, haven't you, love?
Just a walk.

spine.hint: Ines keeps steering the talk to Leo's walk; Rook tells her to leave it; Tom is curious.

probe.ask: Ines, where am I going tomorrow, do you reckon?
Rook, where would I find the old ship's boy?
Tom, is there anyone left alive who sailed on the Halcyon?
Rook, when's Tom taking me out on the boat?

spine.text: Tom goes out to see to his boat.

spine.hint: Ines and Rook talk quietly at the end of the bar while Leo finishes his drink.

spine.text: Goodnight, both.
Leo goes up to bed.
Rook. If he goes to Ropewalk tomorrow, I want to know which door.
Then follow him yourself.

spine.hint: Ines plots how to find out which house it is; Rook won't help.

spine.scene: A street of narrow houses, early morning

spine.text: Early morning. Leo walks up Ropewalk Row in the drizzle, counting doors. Rook, out with his barrow of nets, watches from the corner, too far off to hear anything.
Leo stops at a blue door halfway up, knocks twice, and waits. After a long while the door opens and he goes in.
*To himself.* Blue door. So that's who.
Back on the quay, Ines is waiting by the fish shed with tea and an expression.
Well?
Went to a door on the Row. Blue one.
The blue door! That's old Sefton's. Who'd have thought it.

spine.hint: Ines is delighted with herself; Rook regrets saying anything.
Ines wonders what an old man could tell Leo; Rook tells her to mind her own business.
Rook goes back to his nets.

probe.ask: Ines, which house did I go to this morning?
Rook, what's the old man's address, exactly?
Mira, remind me where the old ship's boy lives?
